Proprioception enables self-modeling through internal representations of body state, while exteroception allows interaction with the environment. These dual pathways form the basis of closed-loop control, where sensory data informs motor output in real time. In GSI, this translates to Bayesian belief updating across multimodal sensory inputs, whereas in GSE, it manifests as dynamic state transitions driven by integrated sensorimotor feedback. The failure modes arise when either pathway becomes compromised—either through loss of proprioceptive integrity or degradation of sensory fidelity—which disrupts the closed-loop structure essential for adaptive behavior.
